meta.boardNote: The shop prices its menu on two hand-lettered poster boards on the wall: noodles run from #01, and the cold counter from #20. Every item, number, Chinese name, printed English name and price below was transcribed from photographs of those boards — nothing here is estimated.
sources: The shop's own noodle board, photographed by Nosh Nepal and published on the Kungfu Noodles listing (noshnepal.com/restaurant/kungfu-noodles, menu photo 1): items 01, 02, 03, 08, 09, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 25.
The shop's own cold-counter board, photographed by Nosh Nepal and published on the same listing (menu photo 2): items 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 31, 32, 34 and 36.

Google Maps listing for Kungfu Noodles (4.0 from 739 reviews, 1,200 photos): review topics and review text confirming #1, #8, #11, #14, #15, #16, the fried egg, peanuts, cucumber, tripe, pork ears and buff tongue.
Tripadvisor listing d13462947 (4.5 from 21 reviews) and its photo captions: 三鲜蔬菜面, 凉拌猪头肉, 盐水花生, 番茄鸡蛋面, 卤肉牛肉面, 凉拌牛舌.
myRepublica feature “Land of noodles — Sincerely from China”: 15 noodle dishes and 20 sides, handmade noodles, ingredients imported from China, pork paws and buff tongue among the sides.
meta.note: The board carries more numbers than we could read — the photographs cut off or blur a few tiles. Anything we could not read is left off the site rather than guessed at.

categories.name: Noodles
categories.blurb: Handmade noodles, cooked to order. The number on the left is printed on the board in the shop — say the number and you get exactly this bowl.

items.name: Kungfu Noodles Special
items.desc: The bowl the shop is named for: buff, chilli and Chinese sauce in a noodle soup. The feature written about it calls it hot, spicy, meaty and chewy.
items.source: Noodle board #01 — “Kungfu noodles-Special” 350, printed ingredients “buff, chilli, chinese sauce, noodle & soup”, two flames. Confirmed by the Google review topic “Special Kungfu Noodles” and by myRepublica.

items.name: Noodles with Chicken Gizzard
items.desc: Chicken gizzard and chilli in a noodle soup. Two flames on the board.
items.source: Noodle board #02 — “Noodles with chicken gizzard” 320, printed ingredients “chicken gizzard, chilli, noodles & soup”.

items.name: Noodles, Sichuan Style
items.desc: Minced meat and vegetables in a noodle soup, built on Sichuan pepper — numbing more than simply hot.
items.source: Noodle board #03 — “Noodles, Sichuan Style” 320, printed ingredients “Minced meat, Vegts, noodle & Soup”. Named in Tripadvisor reviews.

items.name: Noodles with Chicken & Mushroom
items.desc: Chicken and mushroom in a Chinese-sauce noodle soup. A regular who has eaten here since 2018 calls this the bowl to order, especially in winter.
items.source: Noodle board #08 — “Noodles with chicken & mushroom” 320, printed ingredients “mushroom, chicken, chinese sauce, noodles & soup”. Confirmed by a Google review: “My favorite would be the #8, which is chicken noodle… served with chicken and mushroom.”

items.name: Special Chinese Dry Noodles
items.desc: No broth: dry noodles with pickled mustard tuber, peanuts and minced meat.
items.source: Noodle board #09 — “Special Chinese Dry Noodles” 320, printed ingredients “pickled mustard tuber, peanuts, meat, dry noodles”, one flame. Also described in the Tripadvisor feature.

items.name: Noodles with Super Spicy Chicken
items.desc: Spicy chicken and peanuts over dry noodles. Three flames on the board — the hottest thing printed on it.
items.source: Noodle board #11 — “Noodles with super spicy chicken” 320, printed ingredients “spicy chicken, peanuts, dry noodles”, three flames. Confirmed by Google reviews naming “#11”.

items.name: Noodles, Beijing Style
items.desc: Minced meat, cucumber and carrot over dry noodles — the mild, savoury one.
items.source: Noodle board #12 — “Noodles, Beijing Style” 320, printed ingredients “Minced meat, cucumber, carrot, dry noodles”.

items.name: Noodles with Three Vegetables
items.desc: Mushroom, tomato and spinach in a Chinese-sauce noodle soup. The board marks this one “For Vegetarian”.
items.source: Noodle board #13 — “Noodles with 3 vegs. For Vegetarian” 320, printed ingredients “mushroom, tomato, spinach, chinese sauce, noodle & soup”. Also captioned 三鲜蔬菜面 on Tripadvisor.

items.name: Noodles, Wuhan Style
items.desc: Sesame sauce, vegetables and dry noodles — no broth, no meat printed on the board. Toss it hard before the first bite.
items.source: Noodle board #14 — “Noodles, Wuhan Style” 320, printed ingredients “Sesame sauce, vegetables, dry noodles”, two flames. A Google reviewer orders “#14 Noodles, Wuhan Style and a fried egg”.

items.name: Noodles, Chongqing Style
items.desc: Chilli, peanuts and Chinese sauce in a noodle soup. Three flames on the board.
items.source: Noodle board #15 — “Noodles, Chongqing Style” 320, printed ingredients “chilli, peanuts, chinese sauce, noodles & soup”, three flames. Google reviewers order “no. 15 and 16” together.

items.name: Hot & Sour Noodles
items.desc: Chilli, peanuts and Chinese sauce in a noodle soup — sour first, then the numbing heat. Three flames.
items.source: Noodle board #16 — “Hot & Sour Noodles” 320, printed ingredients “chilli, peanuts, chinese sauce, noodle & soup”, three flames (the Tripadvisor reviewer rates this one as the vegetarian-friendly order).

categories.name: Cold Counter & Sides
categories.blurb: The cold counter across the back wall, numbered from #20. Order two or three for the table while the noodles are cooked.

items.name: Cold Sliced Tomato
items.desc: Sliced tomato, dressed cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #20 — “tomato” 150.

items.name: Salted Peanuts
items.desc: Boiled peanuts in brine — the bowl that lands on every table.
items.source: Cold-counter board #21 — “peanuts” 150. Also captioned 盐水花生 on Tripadvisor and named in Google reviews.

items.name: Preserved Egg with Green Pepper
items.desc: Century egg chopped with green pepper.
items.source: Cold-counter board #22 — “preserved egg” 150. The client brief also lists preserved egg among the shop's sides.

items.name: Cold Onion Salad
items.desc: Raw onion, dressed cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #23 — “onion” 150.

items.name: Pickled Chicken Paws
items.desc: Chicken feet cured in pickled mountain pepper.
items.source: Cold-counter board #24 — “chicken paw” 240.

items.name: Fried Egg
items.desc: A fried egg on top of any bowl. Both boards print it — it is the cheapest thing in the shop.
items.source: Printed on both boards, #25 — “Fried egg” 100. A Google reviewer pairs it with “#14 Noodles, Wuhan Style”.

items.name: Spiced Chicken
items.desc: Chicken braised in the shop's spiced master stock, served cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #26 — “spiced chicken” 240.

items.name: Five-Spice Chicken Gizzard
items.desc: Gizzard braised with five spice and sliced cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #27 — “chicken gizzard” 240.

items.name: Spiced Buff
items.desc: Buff braised in five spice and sliced cold — what the reviews call the buff salad.
items.source: Cold-counter board #28 — “spiced buff” 240. The Google listing's review topics name “buff salad” seven times.

items.name: Pork Ear in Chilli Oil
items.desc: Thin slices of pork ear under chilli oil — all crunch.
items.source: Cold-counter board #31 — “pork ear meat” 240. Tripadvisor reviewers list pig's ears among the sides.

items.name: Cold Pork Tripe
items.desc: Pork tripe dressed cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #32 — “pork tripe” 240. Google reviews name tripe among the sides.

items.name: Braised Pork Paws
items.desc: Pork trotters braised until sticky, served cold.
items.source: Cold-counter board #34 — “pork paws” 240. myRepublica names pork paws as one of the shop's not-so-typical sides.

items.name: Five-Spice Buff Tongue
items.desc: Buff tongue, five spice, sliced thin.
items.source: Cold-counter board #36 — “buff tongue” 240. Named by myRepublica and captioned 凉拌牛舌 on Tripadvisor.

unlisted.title: Also on the wall
unlisted.body: The two boards carry more numbers than are printed here — the photographs cut off part of the cold counter and blurred a few noodles. They are left out rather than guessed at. There are cold bottles and cans in the fridge by the counter too; ask at the till for what is in it that day.
